meta.title: FORGE — Strength + Hypertrophy Library (Full Gym Equipment, Combat-Athlete Off-Season/GPP)

Novice.rest_note: Add 15-30s to all rest times below — technique and recovery come before density.
Novice.notes: Master the movement pattern with strict form before chasing load or fatigue. No drop sets, no rest-pause, no training to failure.

Beginner.notes: Standard straight-set progression. Add a paused rep variant on the last set of one exercise per session to build positional strength.

Intermediate.rest_note: Use rest times as written; supersets may share rest windows.
Intermediate.notes: Volume becomes the main lever for hypertrophy work — add sets before adding load once a rep target is consistently hit.

methods_allowed: drop sets (hypertrophy bias, isolation-adjacent movements only)
Advanced.rest_note: Use rest times as written; rest-pause/drop sets compress the last set only.
Advanced.notes: Individualize volume by recovery capacity — this population usually needs LESS added volume than programs default to, not more, once fatigue from skill training is accounted for.

methods_allowed: accommodating resistance (strength bias, where rack allows)
Elite.rest_note: Autoregulated — written rest times are a floor, not a target.
Elite.notes: Strength/hypertrophy work is a supporting block (off-season/GPP), not the priority — kept low-fatigue enough that it never competes with skill-training quality that week.

Strength-Bias.notes: Load is the priority lever. Reps stay low enough that bar speed doesn't degrade.

Hypertrophy-Bias.intensity: 60-75% e1RM, RPE 7-9 (last 1-2 sets near failure from Intermediate up)
Hypertrophy-Bias.tempo: 3-4s eccentric, brief pause, controlled concentric — under tension, not rushed
Hypertrophy-Bias.notes: Volume (hard sets per muscle per week) and proximity to failure are the priority levers, not absolute load.

Hybrid.notes: Compounds run strength-style rep ranges, accessories run hypertrophy-style rep ranges within the same session.

global_rules: This library is a GENERAL strength/hypertrophy tool, not fight-specific power or conditioning work — use it in off-season/GPP blocks, not in-camp, for combat-sport athletes, or as a standalone program for any lifter.

Strength-Bias = load is the priority lever (low reps, high %1RM, long rest). Hypertrophy-Bias = volume and proximity to failure are the priority levers (higher reps, shorter rest, tempo control). Hybrid runs compounds strength-style and accessories hypertrophy-style in the same session.

Progression rule: on Strength-Bias, add load once every prescribed rep is hit with 1-2 reps in reserve. On Hypertrophy-Bias, add ONE set before adding load, once every prescribed rep is hit for all sets.

For combat athletes specifically: hypertrophy blocks belong in the off-season or early GPP phase of a camp, not the final 6-8 weeks before competition — mass gained close to fight week works against making weight and against speed/conditioning.

With full gym equipment: compound free-weight lifts (squat/hinge/press/row variants) stay the FIRST exercise of every session regardless of level — machines and cables are used to finish a muscle group with controlled fatigue after the compound, not to replace it. This keeps the movement-quality standard from the simple-equipment version while adding the isolation options a full gym makes possible.

Machines/cables are the preferred tool for taking a set close to true failure (Hypertrophy-Bias, Advanced/Elite) since they remove the stabilization demand that limits how safely a free-weight set can be pushed that far.
Deload every 4th week: cut sets by ~40% at the same intensity, all levels.
Antagonist-pairing supersets (chest+back, biceps+triceps) are the default way to add training density without adding session length once superset methods are unlocked (Intermediate+).

Reverse Hyper appears in both posterior_chain and glutes pools deliberately — it is genuinely effective for both and also doubles as a light recovery tool (bodyweight pendulum, high reps) on non-lifting days.

Elite-level athletes should treat this entire library as a low-fatigue supporting block — if hypertrophy work is making the next day's skill session feel worse, cut the set count, not the skill session.
